t: It was the single largest battle of the war and the largest in the world since Leipzig in 1813, with around 285,000 Prussian troops against 240,000 Austrians on the Bohemian front.

Almost all the fighting on the Prussian side was done by the First Army and one guards division of the Second, and the Prussian needle gun, a breechloader, outpaced the Austrian muzzleloaders in rate of fire.
The Prussian victory cleared a path to German unification without Austria and left Prussia a free hand when war with France came in 1870.
dyk: Austria had refused to sign the First Geneva Convention, so its medical personnel counted as combatants and withdrew with the army, leaving the wounded on the field. Over 900 lay without care until the Saxon nurse Marie Simon arrived several days later.
ev: The Army of the Elbe advances to Dresden and defeats the Saxon army of 23,000
Benedek reluctantly moves his army out of Olmütz
Moltke orders the First and Second Armies to Jitschin
Prince Friedrich Karl defeats the Austrian I Corps at Jitschin
The Prussian armies defeat Benedek's army between Sadová and Königgrätz
The last skirmish is fought at Blumenau as the Peace of Prague is being signed
The French ambassador presents Bismarck with a demand to relinquish Mainz
War with France, in whose background lay the French demand for revenge for Sadová

f.place: Near the Bohemian city of Hradec Králové (Königgrätz) and the village of Sadová, between the Bystřice and the Elbe, now in the Czech Republic
f.sides: The Kingdom of Prussia under King Wilhelm I, with the Army of the Elbe (39,000) under Herwarth von Bittenfeld, the First Army (85,000) under Prince Friedrich Karl and the Second Army (almost 100,000) under Crown Prince Frederick William, against the Austrian Empire and its Saxon allies under Ludwig von Benedek, 215,000 men in the battle
f.outcome: The Austrian army was forced to retreat across the Elbe with roughly 31,000 men killed, wounded or missing, against nearly 9,000 on the Prussian side. Prussia went on to win the war.
